name: HDR metadata and muxing tools (dovi_tool, hdr10plus_tool, MP4Box, mkvmerge, FFmpeg color/HDR)
versionDocumented: dovi_tool 2.3.4; hdr10plus_tool 1.7.2; MP4Box - GPAC version 26.07-revrelease; mkvmerge v103.0 ('The Darkness') 64-bit; ffmpeg version 9.0.2
summary: These tools handle HDR signaling and dynamic metadata around an encoder rather than compressing video. dovi_tool and hdr10plus_tool extract, convert, edit, generate and inject Dolby Vision RPUs and HDR10+ SEI in raw HEVC; MP4Box and mkvmerge put the result in MP4 or MKV with the right DV configuration and color boxes; FFmpeg tags, retags and filters color properties and moves streams in and out of Annex B. Strengths: lossless metadata work, no re-encode, scriptable. Weaknesses: they work frame by frame, so frame counts must match exactly, the dynamic-metadata tools only read raw HEVC/MKV, and each tool numbers color values slightly differently.
license: dovi_tool MIT; hdr10plus_tool MIT; GPAC/MP4Box LGPL-2.1-or-later; MKVToolNix GPL-2.0-or-later; FFmpeg GPL-3.0-or-later (this Homebrew build)

hdr.summary: HDR10 needs four things to agree: 10-bit 4:2:0 pixels; VUI tags primaries 9 (BT.2020), transfer 16 (PQ), matrix 9 (BT.2020 NCL), limited range; SEI mastering display (ST 2086) and MaxCLL/MaxFALL; and the same values in the container (MP4 colr nclx + mdcv + clli, or Matroska Colour/MasteringMetadata). HLG uses transfer 18 and usually no mastering SEI. The encoder writes VUI and SEI; FFmpeg frame tags (set with the setparams filter) plus -mastering_display/-content_light side data feed both the encoder and the MP4/MKV muxer; MP4Box (colr, -hdr) and mkvmerge (--color-*, --max-*) can add or fix container values without re-encoding; hevc_metadata/av1_metadata bitstream filters fix VUI tags. HDR10+ and Dolby Vision are layered on afterwards with hdr10plus_tool inject and dovi_tool inject-rpu, then muxed with MP4Box :dvp=8.1 or mkvmerge.
hdr.example: ffmpeg -mastering_display "G(13250,34500)B(7500,3000)R(34000,16000)WP(15635,16450)L(10000000,1)" -content_light 1000,400 -i master.mov -map 0:v:0 -vf setparams=color_primaries=bt2020:color_trc=smpte2084:colorspace=bt2020nc:range=tv -c:v libx265 -pix_fmt yuv420p10le -x265-params "hdr10-opt=1" -tag:v hvc1 out.mp4
pitfalls: FFmpeg 9.0.2 (tested): output -color_primaries/-color_trc on a libx265 encode from an untagged source are overwritten by the frames' unspecified values, so the MP4 gets no colr box and MKV no primaries/transfer, even though x265-params can still write a correct VUI. Tag frames with setparams, and pass -mastering_display/-content_light before -i so mdcv/clli (MP4) or MasteringMetadata (MKV) are written too.
FFmpeg's MP4/MOV muxer writes the colr box only when primaries, transfer and matrix are ALL specified; one missing tag means no container color at all.
FFmpeg drops the dvcC/dvvC box in MP4 unless -strict unofficial is given, so the file silently plays as HDR10.
HEVC in MP4 for Apple should use hvc1 (or dvh1); Apple's HLS spec marks hev1/dvhe as not recommended (rule 1.10). Pass -tag:v hvc1 to FFmpeg.
Raw .hevc has no timing: MP4Box assumes 25 fps without :fps=, mkvmerge needs --default-duration.
RPU and HDR10+ entries map to frames by order. Any trim, frame-rate change or interpolation needs the metadata retimed (dovi_tool editor / hdr10plus_tool editor) or regenerated.
Cropping letterbox bars invalidates DV L5 offsets; use dovi_tool --crop or editor active_area.
MP4Box :nosei strips HDR10 and HDR10+ SEI.
Range numbering differs: FFmpeg color_range 1=tv 2=pc; H.273/bsf 0=limited 1=full; mkvmerge 1=broadcast 2=full 3=derived.
Chroma location numbering differs: FFmpeg = H.273 type + 1.
mkvmerge color coordinates are decimal R,G,B; x265/FFmpeg/HEVC SEI use integers in 0.00002 units ordered G,B,R.
The FFmpeg colorspace filter cannot handle PQ/HLG, and this FFmpeg build has no zscale or libplacebo, so tonemap has no ready linearization step.
Dolby Vision profile 5 has no HDR10 fallback; never strip its RPU expecting a usable HDR10 file.
x265 --repeat-headers puts parameter sets into the samples; it is meant for raw streams without a container, so leave it off for hvc1 MP4 output (x265 docs; Apple HLS rule 1.10).

recipes.name: Inject HDR10+ JSON into an HEVC encode
recipes.goal: Add HDR10+ dynamic metadata to an existing HDR10 HEVC encode
recipes.content: HDR10 HEVC (MP4/MKV) + HDR10+ JSON with one entry per frame
recipes.args: ffmpeg -i encode.mkv -map 0:v:0 -c:v copy -bsf:v hevc_mp4toannexb -f hevc video.hevc && hdr10plus_tool inject -i video.hevc -j hdr10plus.json -o video_hdr10p.hevc && hdr10plus_tool --verify extract video_hdr10p.hevc && mkvmerge -o out.mkv --default-duration 0:24000/1001fps video_hdr10p.hevc -D encode.mkv
recipes.why: hdr10plus_tool only reads Annex B HEVC, so the video is copied out losslessly, injected, verified, then remuxed with the original audio/subtitles. Frame counts of JSON and video must agree; use hdr10plus_tool editor to fix them after trims or frame-rate changes.

recipes.name: Carry HDR10+ from source to a new x265 encode
recipes.goal: Keep the source's HDR10+ when re-encoding at the same frame rate
recipes.args: ffmpeg -i src.mkv -map 0:v:0 -c copy -bsf:v hevc_mp4toannexb -f hevc - | hdr10plus_tool extract -o hdr10plus.json -   (then encode with x265 --dhdr10-info hdr10plus.json, or inject afterwards)
recipes.why: Extraction reorders metadata to presentation order; only add --skip-reorder if the README's misauthoring signs appear.

recipes.name: Convert Dolby Vision profile 7 to 8.1
recipes.goal: Single-layer, HDR10-compatible DV from a UHD Blu-ray dual-layer stream
recipes.content: DV profile 7 (FEL or MEL) HEVC, e.g. an MKV remux
recipes.args: ffmpeg -i input.mkv -map 0:v:0 -c:v copy -bsf:v hevc_mp4toannexb -f hevc - | dovi_tool -m 2 convert --discard - -o BL_RPU.hevc && dovi_tool extract-rpu BL_RPU.hevc -o RPU.bin && dovi_tool info -i RPU.bin -s
recipes.why: -m 2 rewrites each RPU as profile 8.1 and drops the reconstruction mapping; --discard removes the EL, leaving the HDR10 base layer plus RPU. FEL titles lose the enhancement-layer detail (usually small), MEL titles lose nothing visible. The summary check confirms profile 8 and the frame count.

recipes.name: Mux DV 8.1 HEVC into MP4
recipes.goal: MP4 that Apple TV / LG / Sony see as Dolby Vision and others as HDR10
recipes.content: Annex B HEVC with 8.1 RPU (from inject-rpu or convert)
recipes.args: MP4Box -add BL_RPU.hevc:dvp=8.1:fps=24000/1001 -add source.mp4#audio -new out.mp4 && MP4Box -infox out.mp4
recipes.why: Raw HEVC needs an explicit frame rate (MP4Box assumes 25 otherwise), and dvp writes the Dolby Vision configuration box. MP4Box keeps parameter sets out of band (hvc1), which Apple asks for (HLS rule 1.10). FFmpeg alternative: ffmpeg -i in.mkv -map 0 -c copy -tag:v hvc1 -strict unofficial out.mp4 (movenc.c writes dvcC/dvvC only with -strict unofficial).

recipes.name: Mux DV into MKV
recipes.content: Annex B HEVC with RPU, or MP4 with dvh1/dvcC
recipes.why: mkvmerge reads single-layer DV from Annex B elementary streams (v58), reads DV from MP4 files (v57) and combines Blu-ray two-track DV into one track (v81), per NEWS. Raw streams need --default-duration; -D takes only audio/subtitles from the second file.

recipes.name: Generate DV 8.1 from HDR10+ metadata
recipes.goal: Add a DV layer to an HDR10+ title
recipes.args: ffmpeg -i in.mkv -map 0:v:0 -c copy -bsf:v hevc_mp4toannexb -f hevc BL.hevc && hdr10plus_tool extract BL.hevc -o hdr10plus.json && dovi_tool generate -j gen.json --hdr10plus-json hdr10plus.json -o RPU.bin && dovi_tool inject-rpu -i BL.hevc --rpu-in RPU.bin -o BL_RPU.hevc
recipes.why: gen.json (start from assets/generator_examples/default_cmv40.json) supplies profile, length and L6; the HDR10+ data becomes L1. Check frame counts match before injecting.

recipes.name: Encode HDR10 with correct signaling (FFmpeg + libx265)
recipes.goal: HDR10 file with VUI, SEI and container metadata all consistent
recipes.args: ffmpeg -mastering_display "G(13250,34500)B(7500,3000)R(34000,16000)WP(15635,16450)L(10000000,1)" -content_light 1000,400 -i master.mov -map 0:v:0 -vf setparams=color_primaries=bt2020:color_trc=smpte2084:colorspace=bt2020nc:range=tv -c:v libx265 -pix_fmt yuv420p10le -x265-params "hdr10-opt=1" -tag:v hvc1 out.mp4
recipes.why: Tested with FFmpeg 9.0.2 and x265 4.3: setparams tags the frames, so libx265 writes BT.2020/PQ/BT.2020nc limited-range VUI and the muxer writes colr; -mastering_display/-content_light (input options) attach HDR10 side data, which libx265 turns into mastering-display and content-light SEI and the MP4 muxer into mdcv/clli (MKV: Colour and MasteringMetadata). Use the grade's real mastering display and measured MaxCLL/MaxFALL. The older form with only output -color_* options and x265-params master-display/max-cll gives correct SEI and VUI but no container colr/mdcv/clli in this build.

recipes.name: Fix wrong color tags without re-encoding
recipes.goal: Retag an HDR HEVC/AV1 stream that was marked BT.709
recipes.why: Bitstream filters rewrite header fields only, so quality is untouched. They cannot add HDR10 mastering/CLL SEI; add those via -mastering_display/-content_light on re-encode, MP4Box -hdr, or mkvmerge --max-luminance etc. Tested with 9.0.2 (hevc_metadata form, stream copy into MKV).

recipes.name: Verify an HDR file
recipes.goal: Confirm HDR10 / HLG / HDR10+ / DV signaling end to end
recipes.args: ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=codec_tag_string,pix_fmt,color_range,color_space,color_transfer,color_primaries,chroma_location:stream_side_data_list -of json out.mp4 ; ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -read_intervals %+#1 -show_frames -show_entries frame=side_data_list -of json out.mp4 ; ffmpeg -i out.mp4 -map 0:v:0 -c copy -bsf:v hevc_mp4toannexb -f hevc - | hdr10plus_tool --verify extract - ; ffmpeg -i out.mp4 -map 0:v:0 -c copy -bsf:v hevc_mp4toannexb -f hevc - | dovi_tool extract-rpu -l 200 - -o rpu.bin && dovi_tool info -i rpu.bin -s ; MP4Box -infox out.mp4 ; MP4Box -diso out.mp4 -out boxes.xml (or mkvmerge -J out.mkv)
recipes.why: Stream fields show VUI/container tags (expect bt2020 / smpte2084 or arib-std-b67 / bt2020nc / tv, hvc1 or dvh1 tag); stream side data shows DOVI configuration; the first frame's side data shows mastering display, content light and HDR10+; the tools confirm dynamic metadata; MP4Box -infox shows the DV configuration, and the -diso box dump shows colr, mdcv and clli.

recipes.name: Strip Dolby Vision to plain HDR10
recipes.goal: Fallback file for players that mis-handle DV

codeTables.notes: Values verified against FFmpeg's pixfmt.h enums and `MP4Box -h cicp`; MP4Box's cicp list stops at matrix 11 and lacks 12-17 names. MP4Box prints 'SMPTE249' for transfer 7, a typo for SMPTE 240. DV profile 5 tagging is from general knowledge and differs between sources; treat as unverified.

lumoraIntegration.summary: Lumora uses these tools only for dynamic metadata after the encode: ffmpeg -c:v copy -bsf:v hevc_mp4toannexb dumps Annex B; for DV 8.1 it either retimes the source RPU (dovi_tool -m 2 extract-rpu, two editor passes, info -s frame-count check) or generates new metadata (dovi_tool generate -j), then dovi_tool inject-rpu; for HDR10+ it writes its own JSON and runs hdr10plus_tool inject. It remuxes with MP4Box (-add ...:fps=...[:dvp=8.1] -add file#audio -new) for MP4/MOV, mkvmerge (-o, --default-duration 0:num/denfps, -D) otherwise, or FFmpeg -c copy as a last resort. Static HDR10 signaling comes from the CLI encoders' own flags in encoders.json (x265 --master-display/--max-cll/--hdr10/--hdr10-opt, SVT-AV1 --mastering-display, etc.).
gaps: FFmpeg fallback remux to MP4/MOV (ExportEngine) passes neither -tag:v hvc1 nor -strict unofficial: HEVC may be tagged hev1 (Apple playback issue) and any DV loses dvcC. Not verified by running the app.
MP4Box fps is passed as a decimal; 24000/1001 would be exact.
DolbyVisionRetimer reads the frame count as the first integer > 1 in `dovi_tool info -s` output, which depends on the summary layout.

No mkvmerge color/mastering flags are passed; Lumora relies on the bitstream VUI/SEI. Checked with mkvmerge v103: muxing a raw HEVC elementary stream leaves the Matroska Colour fields empty (mkvmerge -J shows no color properties), so MKV players that read only container metadata see no HDR tags.

notes: Scope: every option and subcommand option of dovi_tool 2.3.4 and hdr10plus_tool 1.7.2, and every option in the captured MP4Box (general and import) and mkvmerge help, is listed. For FFmpeg, the options matching color, side data, mastering, HDR, Dolby Vision and the video bitstream filters are listed; audio-only and unrelated bitstream filters (opus_metadata, pcm_rechunk, noise, dv_error_marker, eia608_to_smpte436m, hapqa_extract) are left out, as is the rest of the ~14,000-line help. dovi_tool demux/export/mux/plot/remove help was read by running `dovi_tool <cmd> --help` because the captured help file lacked those sections; MP4Box -info comes from `MP4Box -h dump`. The MP4Box -hdr XML format comes from GPAC source code because no doc describes it. FFmpeg 9.1 adds a side_data bitstream filter that this 9.0.2 build does not have (Changelog). Fact-check 2026-11-12: the HDR10 example, the DV/HDR10+ tool syntax, MP4Box colr/dvp/hdr and mkvmerge -J were run against the installed binaries.
